battle.name: 達爾達尼亞-巴斯塔尼戰爭
battle.theater: 多瑙河下游普魯特河谷
battle.brief: 公元前179年，巴斯塔尼人再越多瑙河南侵達爾達尼亞，達爾達尼亞王向羅馬求援，羅馬執政官率軍團與輔助軍自亞得里亞海北上，與達爾達尼亞聯軍在多瑙河下游擊潰巴斯塔尼，迫其退回河北。卡面秦連弩並不在場，其西方同類為手搖張弦弩與車載弩砲，同樣以蓄力機括換取持續火力。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前二世紀末多瑙河下游的一場跨界衝突，參戰方是中部巴爾幹的達爾達尼亞王國、多瑙河與喀爾巴阡山之間的巴斯塔尼人，以及以盟友身分介入的羅馬。達爾達尼亞人居住在上內雷特瓦河、科索沃平原、西莫特利察河谷一帶，政治形態是若干城邦與部落組成的聯盟，由國王統轄，另有貴族議事與城邦議會並存；主要城邑有斯庫皮、特蘭達、烏爾皮亞納、多克萊、拜利斯與阿曼提亞。其兵制以步兵為主，部族首領各自領兵，鎧甲與錢幣都帶有馬其頓的痕跡：他們鑄造仿腓力二世式銀斯塔特，用以支付雇傭兵的價錢並維持城邦聯盟的開銷。巴斯塔尼人是住在多瑙河以北、喀爾巴阡山與黑海之間的一支大族，部族分支眾多，有佩烏基尼、阿特莫尼等名號，國王是權力核心，國內以長劍騎兵與持大盾的步兵作戰骨幹，一向在多瑙河兩岸維持橋頭堡，藉掠奪相鄰地區補充兵員與糧食。羅馬一方由執政官統率的兩個軍團為主，輔以行省與盟邦提供的輔助軍、騎兵與工兵隊；羅馬並非以征服為目標，而以阻斷巴斯塔尼南進、把防線釘在多瑙河一線為務，與達爾達尼亞的聯盟以條約與人質維持。至於戰役的具體經過，存世文字集中於李維《羅馬史》第四十卷，其餘多為片斷，記錄有限。
countriesEn: This war was a cross-border conflict fought in the lower Danube in the late second century BC, between the kingdom of the Dardani in the central Balkans, the Bastarnae who lived between the Danube and the Carpathian Mountains, and Rome, which entered as an ally. The Dardani were the people of the upper Neretva, the Kosovo plain and the Toplica valley, and their political form was a league of cities and clans ruled by a king, with an aristocracy and the councils of the cities alongside him; their chief settlements were Scupi, Theranda, Ulpiana, Doclea, Byllis and Amantia. Their military system rested on infantry, each clan leader commanding his own men, and both their armour and their coinage carried the mark of Macedon: they struck silver staters imitating those of Philip II, which paid the price of mercenary wages and kept the league of cities supplied. The Bastarnae were a great people settled north of the Danube, between the Carpathians and the Black Sea, divided into numerous branches, among them the Peucini and the Atmoni, with the king as the centre of power; long-sworded cavalry and infantry carrying large shields formed the core of their fighting, and they habitually maintained bridgeheads on both banks of the river, taking what they needed from the neighbouring country by raid. Rome came with two legions under a consular commander, supplemented by auxiliaries, cavalry and engineer teams drawn from the provinces and the allied communities; Rome was not aiming at conquest but at breaking the southern thrust of the Bastarnae and pinning the line of defence on the Danube itself, and the alliance between Rome and Dardania was held in being by treaty and by hostages. As for the course of the campaign itself, the surviving text is concentrated in the fortieth book of Livy's History of Rome and the rest is fragmentary: the record is limited.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物不多，且多半出自羅馬一側。巴斯塔尼方面的國王克隆迪庫斯最為人知：公元前181年，他率部眾越過多瑙河、直抵亞得里亞海沿岸，接待羅馬元老院派來的兩名使節，史家記為 Marcus Aemilius Scaurus 與 Lucius Cornelius Dolabella；他在會談中聲稱自己並非蓄意來犯，而要為部眾爭取公道，並開出代價高昂的條件。羅馬執政官昆圖斯·富爾維奧斯·諾比略當年率軍與之對峙，兩軍先在希斯特里亞河畔交手，羅馬騎兵一度失利，步兵列陣後才扭轉局面，國王被俘，羅馬隨後給他自由，但要求他交出部分族人作人質並停止南進。達爾達尼亞方面的國王莫努尼奧斯出現在另一端的條約裡：羅馬拒絕單方面支付金錢給巴斯塔尼人，轉而向伊利利亞與達爾達尼亞方向爭取盟友，與這位國王訂下條約，達爾達尼亞人自此成為羅馬在東地中海側的支點。公元前179年率軍進入伊利利亞的羅馬執政官，是整場戰事中真正推動進攻的人；達爾達尼亞一方的部族首領則多數沒有留下名字，他們的作用是把熟悉山口與渡口的地形優勢交給聯軍，而真正決定渡河與合戰時機的，仍是那位遠在羅馬的執政官。
peopleEn: Few of the decisive figures are named, and most of them come from the Roman side. The best known of the Bastarnae is their king Clondicus: in 181 BC he led his people across the Danube as far as the coast of the Adriatic and received two envoys sent by the Roman senate, recorded by the historians as Marcus Aemilius Scaurus and Lucius Cornelius Dolabella; in the talks he said that he had not come to make war, but to obtain justice for his people, and he set out terms that were costly to meet. The Roman consul Quintus Fulvius Nobilior confronted him with the army in that year; the two sides first met on the river Histria, where the Roman cavalry was at first worsted, and only after the infantry had closed up in formation did the tide turn, the king was taken prisoner, and Rome then set him free, on condition that he give up some of his people as hostages and stop the southern advance. The Dardanian king Monunius appears at the other end of the story, in the treaty: Rome refused to pay the Bastarnae money outright and instead sought allies among the Illyrians and the Dardani, concluding a treaty with this king, and from that moment the Dardani became a pivot of Rome in the eastern Mediterranean. The Roman consul who led the army into Illyria in 179 BC is the man who actually drove the offensive forward; most of the Dardanian clan leaders left no name behind, and their part was to hand over their knowledge of the passes and the fords to the allied army, while the moment of crossing and of joining battle was still decided by the consul far away in Rome.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是秦連弩：弩機以蹼板與曲柄把拉力儲存起來，矢匣一次容納數十支至百餘支短矢，踏下踏桿即完成一次上弦與發射，射程約百步上下，專為守城、守壘與壓制密集隊形而設，形制見於《墨子》守城諸篇與戰國末至秦漢的弩機出土件。它並沒有出現在公元前179年的巴爾幹戰場上，這一點必須先講清楚；在此代表的是把射速、持續火力與低操作技術合而為一的機械弩機譜系。同時代地中海世界與之最接近的是希臘式的張力弩（cheiroballista）：以扭力儲能、機匣供箭，由數人合力上弦，一次齊射的箭幕足以封住城門前的通道；羅馬把它裝上兩輪車身成為車載弩砲（carroballista），結構與操作方式可由維特魯維《建築十書》第十卷的描述與柱上浮雕互相印證，但那已是公元前1世紀的成熟形態，公元前179年尚無實物憑據。真正在多瑙河下游開火的是達爾達尼亞與巴斯塔尼的舊式投射武器：達爾達尼亞步兵以短刺槍、小圓盾與青銅頭矛為主，另有大量投石手，採以皮條兜網的石彈；巴斯塔尼人配長劍、大橢圓盾、鐵盔與鎖子甲，用長矛與投槍構成步兵骨幹，騎兵乘體型小而耐跑的馬，善於射擊與迂迴。雙方都沒有可持續供應的重型攻城器械，營帳與輜重靠牛車，糧食多就地徵集與擄掠。
kitsEn: The item on the card is the Qin repeating crossbow: its lock stores the pull of the bow on a plate-and-crank mechanism, the magazine holds several dozen to more than a hundred short bolts at a time, and stepping on the treadle completes cocking and release in a single movement, with a range of about a hundred paces; it was built for the defence of walls and of strongpoints and for pressing dense attacking formations, and its form is known from the siege chapters of the Mohist text and from excavated locks of the late Warring States and the Qin-Han period. It did not appear on the Balkan battlefield of 179 BC, and that has to be said plainly: here it stands for the family of mechanical bolt-throwers that trades rate of fire, sustained fire and low skill of operation in a single machine. The nearest equivalent in the Mediterranean world of the same time is the Greek cheiroballista, which stored energy in twisted skeins, fed its bolts from a case, was cocked by several men together, and whose massed volley was enough to seal the ground in front of a city gate; the Romans put such a weapon on a two-wheeled carriage and made it the carroballista, whose structure and handling can be checked against the description in the tenth book of Vitruvius and against the reliefs on columns, but that is the mature form of the first century BC, and for 179 BC there is no physical evidence for it. What actually put arrows and stones into the air in the lower Danube were the older missiles of the Dardani and the Bastarnae: Dardanian infantry carried short thrusting spears, small round shields and bronze-headed javelins, and there were many slingers using stones in a leather pouch; the Bastarnae had long swords, large oval shields, iron helmets and mail, with spears and javelins forming the backbone of their infantry, while their cavalry rode small and hardy horses and were practised at shooting and turning. Neither side possessed heavy siege engines that could be supplied in quantity; their tents and baggage went on ox-carts, and their food was taken from the country as they went or carried off by raid.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術樣貌，可以從三方的地形選擇推想。達爾達尼亞人熟悉中部巴爾幹的崎嶇山道與石灰岩峽谷，慣於避開開闊平原上的正面交鋒：步兵踞守山口的石築堡壘與村寨高處，以投石手壓制敵方隊形，標槍手在坡下射擊，等對方逼近至投擲距離才以短兵相接；騎兵只用於襲擾糧道與遮斷退路，計畫中的第二次行動不求殲滅，而求把敵人拖回多瑙河北。巴斯塔尼人自北岸南下，慣於以大隊騎兵在開闊地正面衝撞，再以步兵縱隊接續展開，其弱點正在於一旦離開平原進入山道，馬力與投射物都難以施展。羅馬軍隊的打法則是另一套：步兵立於密集縱隊，以重裝中兵在前、輕裝兵與標槍兵分列兩翼，騎兵布於陣後與營地四野；每到一處宿營必挖壕、築土壘、置柵，形成方整的營盤，行軍時以縱隊通過狹窄地形，遇到敵騎即收束成圓陣。雙方聯合作戰的要點，是由達爾達尼亞嚮導引導羅馬騎兵與輔助軍切斷多瑙河沿線的渡口與草料場，使巴斯塔尼的補給船隊無法靠岸；一旦對方失去渡河點與牧場，前鋒便不得不脫離掩體回撤。遠程火力在這場戰役裡並非壓倒性的因素，羅馬方面的弩砲數量有限，真正決定戰果的是投射物落點、河谷渡口與退路三件事的配合。
tacticsEn: The shape of this war can be read from the choices of ground made by the three parties. The Dardani knew the broken mountain tracks and limestone gorges of the central Balkans and were used to avoiding a set-piece clash on open plain: their infantry occupied stone-built strongpoints and the heights of villages at the mouths of passes, pressed the enemy's formations with slingers, shot javelins from below the slope and only closed at close quarters when the other side had come within throwing distance; their cavalry was used to harrow supply lines and cut the way of retreat, and the second stage of the operation was designed not to destroy the enemy but to drag it back north of the Danube. The Bastarnae came down from the north bank accustomed to charging with large bodies of cavalry across open ground and then extending in infantry columns behind them, and their weakness lay precisely in the fact that once they left the plain for the mountain tracks neither horsepower nor missiles could be brought to bear. The Roman method was another set of rules: the infantry stood in dense columns, the armoured spearmen in front with light troops and javelin-men on the flanks, the cavalry posted behind the line and around the camp; at every place where it halted the army dug a trench, threw up a rampart and set out a fence to form a square camp, on the march it passed narrow ground in column and closed into a circle when the enemy's horse appeared. The point of the joint operation was for the Dardanian guides to lead the Roman cavalry and auxiliaries to the fords and the grazing grounds along the Danube so that the Bastarnae supply boats could not put in; once the other side had lost its crossings and its pastures, the van had no choice but to break off and withdraw from cover. Missile fire was not the decisive factor in this campaign; the Romans had only a limited number of bolt-throwers, and what decided the result was the combination of where the missiles fell, of the fords in the river valleys, and of the lines of retreat.
data: 可依據的數字大致如下。時間上，戰役屬公元前179年，即李維《羅馬史》第四十卷所載之年；該卷起於公元前181年羅馬與巴斯塔尼的接觸，止於公元前178年，故巴斯塔尼戰線的整段衝突橫跨約三年。規模方面，羅馬按雙執政官遠征的常例，每次出動兩個軍團，軍團步兵各約四千五百至五千五百人，輔以行省與盟邦提供的輔助軍，總兵力在二萬上下，騎兵約二千；此類數目為編制通例，具體到每一年略有出入。巴斯塔尼與達爾達尼亞的兵力，古代作家只給出大族、眾多一類的定性描述，具體數目已不可考，李維在記敘巴斯塔尼國王時亦只寫軍勢盛大而不列數字。地理上，達爾達尼亞的核心區（斯庫皮、科索沃平原一帶）距多瑙河下游約二百五十至三百公里，羅馬軍自亞得里亞海沿岸的利蘇斯一線東進，或沿多瑙河谷地北上；戰線沿多瑙河下游的普魯特河與蘇利納河一帶展開，古代作家所稱的希斯特里亞河，一般認為即今普魯特河一線。武器數據上，希臘式張力弩的重矢約重一公斤上下，有效射程數百步，一次齊射可覆蓋正面數十步；秦連弩的矢匣容數十至百餘支短矢，射程約百步，須一至二人操作，優勢在持續而非單發威力。天候上，多瑙河下游冬季結冰、春夏泥濘，入秋後水位上漲，車隊與騎兵的行動都受河流節奏牽制。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. In time, the campaign belongs to 179 BC, the year recorded in the fortieth book of Livy's History of Rome; that book opens with the contact between Rome and the Bastarnae in 181 BC and runs to 178 BC, so that the whole stretch of conflict on the Bastarnae front ran for about three years. In size, Rome followed the standing practice for a consular campaign, sending out two legions, each of something between four and a half and five and a half thousand foot, together with auxiliaries provided by the provinces and the allied communities, for a total of about twenty thousand men with roughly two thousand horse; such figures are a matter of normal establishment and vary a little from year to year. The strength of the Bastarnae and of the Dardani is known to the ancient writers only in qualitative terms, as a great and numerous people, and the exact numbers are irrecoverable; Livy, writing of the Bastarnae king, says only that his force was great and gives no figure. In geography, the core of Dardania, the region of Scupi and the Kosovo plain, lies some two hundred and fifty to three hundred kilometres from the lower Danube; the Roman army came east from the Adriatic coast by way of Lissus, or north along the Danube valley, and the line of operations ran along the Prut and the Siret in the lower Danube, the river Histria of the ancient writers being generally identified with the Prut. On weapons, the heavy bolt of the Greek cheiroballista weighed about a kilogramme, its effective range was several hundred paces, and a single volley covered some dozens of paces of front; the magazine of the Qin repeating crossbow held several dozen to more than a hundred short bolts, its range was about a hundred paces, it needed one or two men to work, and its advantage lay in sustained fire rather than in the weight of a single shot. On weather, the lower Danube freezes in winter, the ground turns to mud in spring and summer, and the water rises in autumn, so that the movements of the wagon trains and of the cavalry were tied to the rhythm of the river.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是巴斯塔尼的南擴壓力：這支部族在多瑙河北站穩之後，頻頻越河進入伊利利亞與達爾達尼亞的邊境地帶，公元前181年甚至直抵亞得里亞海，距離義大利僅一水之隔，羅馬元老院因此把它視為直接威脅，遣使交涉；使節團開出的條件被羅馬拒絕，羅馬遂不付代價，改為拉攏對方的鄰居。第二層是達爾達尼亞自己的利害：巴斯塔尼的每一次南進都壓在達爾達尼亞王國的東境與通往亞得里亞海、薩洛尼卡方向的商路上，這條路上走的是鹽、琥珀、牲畜與金屬，達爾達尼亞的城邦同盟要靠它維持雇傭兵與造幣的開支；同時達爾達尼亞正面臨馬其頓的壓力，其城邦在公元前二世紀接連被希臘將領掃蕩，王室的正統性正在消耗。羅馬用得着達爾達尼亞的地方也正在這裡：達爾達尼亞人熟悉伊利利亞的山道，願意引導羅馬騎兵封鎖渡口，這是外軍最缺的東西。第三層才是直接導火線：公元前179年前後，巴斯塔尼再度大舉越河並攻入達爾達尼亞與其盟友的地盤，達爾達尼亞向羅馬求援，羅馬執政官率軍進入伊利利亞，戰事遂由邊境衝突升級為聯軍行動。
causeEn: There are three layers of reason. The outermost is the pressure of the Bastarnae expansion to the south: once settled north of the Danube this people crossed the river again and again into the border country of Illyria and Dardania, and in 181 BC they came as far as the Adriatic, only a stretch of water from Italy, so that the Roman senate took them for a direct threat and sent envoys to treat with them; the conditions the envoys proposed were refused, and rather than pay the price Rome turned to making allies of the enemy's neighbours. The second layer is the interest of Dardania itself: every southern push by the Bastarnae pressed on the eastern frontier of the Dardanian kingdom and on the trade road leading to the Adriatic and to Salonica, a road that carried salt, amber, cattle and metal, on which the league of Dardanian cities depended to pay its mercenaries and to keep the mint working; at the same time Dardania faced pressure from Macedon, whose cities were being carried through by Greek commanders in the second century BC, so that the authority of the royal house was being spent. What Rome wanted from Dardania lay in the same place: the Dardani knew the tracks of Illyria and were willing to lead Roman cavalry to the fords, and that was the one thing an outside army most lacked. The third layer is the immediate occasion: about 179 BC the Bastarnae crossed the river again in force and entered the territory of Dardania and its allies, Dardania appealed to Rome for help, the Roman consul led his army into Illyria, and what had been a border clash became a campaign by a coalition.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接影響，是巴斯塔尼的南進被打斷，達爾達尼亞的東境得以喘息，多瑙河以北的橋頭堡格局維持了一段時間；羅馬則在東地中海一側取得一個可靠的盟友與嚮導，學到在沒有地中海航線的情況下如何從陸路深入伊利利亞。往後看，這場仗是羅馬在巴爾幹推展的連串步驟中的前一步：幾年後的第三次馬其頓戰爭中，羅馬正是利用達爾達尼亞在馬其頓後方的不停襲擾，使腓力五世無法全力應付前線；公元前168年皮德納之戰後，羅馬在伊利利亞設立行省，把原本自治的達爾達尼亞各城邦編入新的稅收與兵役體系，其仿腓力二世式銀幣的發行也隨之收斂，國王權威逐步瓦解。巴斯塔尼人退回多瑙河與喀爾巴阡山之間，轉向黑海與多瑙河三角洲求取資源，同羅馬維持時戰時和的關係，直到奧古斯都時代再因北向政策而被卷入戰端，最終以行省人口的形式被編入帝國邊界。長遠看，這場戰爭還有一層方法上的意義：它顯示羅馬在東方的戰爭是聯盟加少量正規軍的典型形態，戰果往往取決於當地部族願意提供多少嚮導與情報，而不是取決於野戰本身。
impactEn: The direct effect of the war was that the southern advance of the Bastarnae was broken, the eastern frontier of Dardania was given room to breathe, and the arrangement of bridgeheads north of the Danube held for a time; Rome in turn gained a dependable ally and a source of guides on the eastern Mediterranean side, and learned how to penetrate inland into Illyria by land when no sea route was available. Looking further ahead, this battle was one step in the chain of Roman advances in the Balkans: in the Third Macedonian War a few years later it was precisely the unremitting pressure of the Dardani on the rear of Macedon that kept Philip V from committing everything to his front; after the battle of Pydna in 168 BC Rome set up the province of Illyria and drew the formerly autonomous Dardanian cities into a new system of taxation and military service, and the issuing of silver in imitation of Philip II came to an end as the authority of the Dardanian king fell away. The Bastarnae withdrew between the Danube and the Carpathians, turned to the Black Sea and the Danube delta for their resources, and kept a relationship with Rome that was war and peace in turns, until the policies of the north under Augustus drew them into a war once more and they were finally absorbed into the frontier of the empire as the population of a province. In the longer term the war carries a lesson of method: it shows that Roman war in the east took the typical form of an alliance with a small number of regular troops, and that the result turned far more on how much guidance and intelligence the local tribes would give than on the field battle itself.
result: 打到公元前179年夏末，勝負已經分明。巴斯塔尼人被擠出達爾達尼亞的東境，在多瑙河下游一線失去可依賴的渡口與牧場，前鋒一旦被切斷便只能收縮；聯軍乘勢驅趕，迫使對方丟下營盤與輜重，渡河北撤。羅馬沒有追過多瑙河，這是共和國在邊界上的一貫作風，戰役的目標是解除威脅而不是兼併土地，多瑙河以北從未進入羅馬的征服計畫。依前例，巴斯塔尼國王被扣作人質或交出族人作保，換取停戰；達爾達尼亞國王得到的是邊境喘息與繼續作羅馬盟友的地位，卻也從此被捲入羅馬與馬其頓的角力。同一年的羅馬本土，執政官回城後正好遇上監察官的改選，公元前179年遂有史書記載的第一批平民出身的監察官，這與邊境戰事同時發生，一邊是羅馬在東方的擴張，一邊是羅馬內部政治的變數。戰後巴斯塔尼與達爾達尼亞在多瑙河一線重新對峙，這條河此後近一個世紀都是雙方的界線；而達爾達尼亞王國本身的終局，則要等到羅馬在皮德納獲勝、伊利利亞行省設立之後才會到來。
resultEn: By the end of the summer of 179 BC the outcome had been decided. The Bastarnae were squeezed out of the eastern frontier of Dardania and, along the lower Danube, lost the fords and the pastures on which they had relied; once their van was cut off it could only contract, and the allied army pressed the advantage, forcing the other side to leave camp and baggage behind and to cross the river northwards. Rome did not pursue beyond the Danube, which was the standing practice of the republic on a frontier: the aim of the campaign was to remove a threat, not to annex territory, and the country north of the Danube had never been part of the Roman plan of conquest. As on the previous occasion the Bastarnae king was kept as a hostage, or gave up some of his people as sureties, in return for a truce; the Dardanian king gained a breathing space on his frontier and the standing of a continued ally of Rome, but from that moment he was also drawn into the quarrel between Rome and Macedon. In the same year at home, the consuls came back to the city just in time for the election of the censors, and 179 BC saw the first censors drawn from the plebeian order of which the histories speak; that took place at the same time as the fighting on the frontier, with Roman expansion in the east on one side and a change in Roman domestic politics on the other. After the war the Bastarnae and the Dardani faced each other again along the Danube, and for nearly a century that river was the line between them; the end of the Dardanian kingdom itself did not come until after the Roman victory at Pydna and the establishment of the province of Illyria.
